conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Effective Nuclear Charge Concept
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Effective Nuclear Charge Concept

summaryBox.title: Z_eff & Shielding
summaryBox.takeaway: Z_eff = Z - σ. Core electrons cancel part of the nuclear charge. Shielding order: s > p > d > f; Penetration: s > p > d > f.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Electrons in multi-electron atoms experience electrostatic attraction to the positively charged nucleus, counterbalanced by electrostatic repulsion from inner-shell electrons (Screening / Shielding Effect):

$$\mathbf{Z_{\text{eff}} = Z - \sigma}$$

where $Z$ is the actual nuclear charge (atomic number) and $\sigma$ is the Slater Screening Constant.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Slater's Rules for Calculating σ
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Slater's Rules for Calculating σ
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SLATER'S RULES SHIELDING GROUPS
                   
   Group electrons: (1s)(2s,2p)(3s,3p)(3d)(4s,4p)(4d)(4f)(5s,5p)...
conceptBreakdown.content:
**A. Target Electron in an s or p Orbital**:
1. Electrons in groups to the right (higher principal shells) contribute **0.00** to $\sigma$.
2. Other electrons in the same $(ns, np)$ group contribute **0.35 each** (exception: in $1s$, other electron contributes **0.30**).
3. All electrons in the $(n-1)$ shell contribute **0.85 each**.
4. All electrons in $(n-2)$ and deeper inner shells contribute **1.00 each**.

**B. Target Electron in a d or f Orbital**:
1. Other electrons in the same $(nd)$ or $(nf)$ group contribute **0.35 each**.
2. All electrons in groups to the left (inner shells + lower subshells) contribute **1.00 each**.

• **Worked Example 1: 4s Electron in Zinc ($Z=30$)**:
$$\text{Zn}: (1s^2)(2s^2 2p^6)(3s^2 3p^6)(3d^{10})(4s^2)$$
- Same group ($4s$): $1 \text{ e}^- \times 0.35 = 0.35$
- $(n-1)$ shell ($n=3$): $18 \text{ e}^- (3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10}) \times 0.85 = 15.30$
- $(n-2)$ and deeper ($n=1,2$): $10 \text{ e}^- \times 1.00 = 10.00$
$$\sigma = 0.35 + 15.30 + 10.00 = \mathbf{25.65} \implies \mathbf{Z_{\text{eff}} = 30 - 25.65 = 4.35}$$

• **Worked Example 2: 3d Electron in Iron ($Z=26$)**:
$$\text{Fe}: (1s^2)(2s^2 2p^6)(3s^2 3p^6)(3d^6)(4s^2)$$
- Higher groups ($4s^2$): $0.00$
- Same group ($3d$): $5 \text{ e}^- \times 0.35 = 1.75$
- Inner groups to the left ($1s,2s,2p,3s,3p = 18\text{ e}^-$): $18 \times 1.00 = 18.00$
$$\sigma = 1.75 + 18.00 = \mathbf{19.75} \implies \mathbf{Z_{\text{eff}} = 26 - 19.75 = 6.25}$$

quickRevision: For s/p electrons: same shell = 0.35 (1s = 0.30), (n-1) = 0.85, (n-2) and deeper = 1.00.
For d/f electrons: same group = 0.35, all inner groups to left = 1.00.
Penetration power: s > p > d > f; Shielding efficiency: s > p > d > f.
Z_eff increases across a period because Z increases by +1 while σ increases by +0.35.
